title: The alcohol flushing response: an unrecognized risk factor for esophageal cancer from alcohol consumption
authors: Brooks PJ, Enoch MA, Goldman D, Li TK, Yokoyama A
funder: The authors received no specific funding for this article.
authorConflicts: The authors have declared that no competing interests exist. Brooks, Enoch and Goldman were at the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism; Brooks and Yokoyama took part in the 2007 IARC Working Group on alcoholic beverage consumption.
result: About 36% of East Asians show facial flushing, nausea and tachycardia after drinking, predominantly from ALDH2 deficiency; at least 540 million people, about 8% of the world population, are estimated to be ALDH2-deficient. In case-control studies from Japan and Taiwan, low-activity ALDH2 heterozygotes who drink have odds ratios of 3.7 to 18.1 for oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma after adjustment for alcohol consumption; ALDH2 deficiency does not influence oesophageal cancer risk in non-drinkers.
